source.title: Data-Efficient Multimodal Fusion on a Single GPU
source.authors: Noël Vouitsis; Zhaoyan Liu; S. Gorti; Valentin Villecroze; Jesse C. Cresswell; Guang-Wei Yu; G. Loaiza-Ganem; M. Volkovs

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports an image-model size sweep and downstream retrieval result, extending the scale–downstream-performance question to multimodal image-text retrieval. It does not test language-model pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling work as background but does not test language-model loss scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. The relevant result is an ablation of unimodal encoder size and Flickr30K retrieval performance.
record.test_reason: This is a multimodal-fusion methods paper; it cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation for model scale. Its one size result is a three-point ablation (Fig. 5a). Frozen DINOv2+BGE encoders are swapped at S/B/L sizes, and the fusion adapters' Flickr30K Recall@1 is reported. That measures how its own method responds to encoder choice, not pretraining-loss scaling. It fits no scaling law and does not test whether downstream gains are predictable from scale or loss. Image and text encoder sizes change together, and the pretraining recipes of the encoders differ. So no version is tested; the finding is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude FuseMix gives compute- and data-efficient multimodal alignment on one GPU, competitive with or beating methods like CLIP. Their ablation shows larger frozen encoders, larger batches and FuseMix augmentation each improve retrieval. They add that dataset quality and diversity matter, not just quantity.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal fusion and retrieval study, not a reproduction of the original language-model loss-scaling measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping larger frozen pretrained image+text encoders (DINOv2 S/B/G with BGE Small/Base/Large) into FuseMix raises Flickr30K text-to-image R@1 monotonically over three points (Fig. 5a, figure-only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream retrieval of lightweight adapters on frozen encoders improves with frozen encoder size.

fits_no_version.finding: More paired image-text data for training the fusion adapters raises Flickr30K R@1 in low-data regimes (Fig. 3a). Data quality matters strongly: about 6x web pairs are needed to match human-annotated pairs (Fig. 3b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adapter-alignment performance grows with paired-data quantity but depends heavily on data quality and diversity.

record.problems: The relevant size-sweep values are available only in a figure in the supplied text, with no uncertainty reported. The size comparison changes both the image and text encoder sizes and concerns one retrieval task; it does not measure language-model loss or fit a scaling law.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape-at-fixed-parameter comparison (fusion adapter depth ablation in App. C is not a fixed-parameter shape test of a pretrained LM).
No power-law fit in any modality; the paired-data quantity sweep (Fig. 3a) is not fit and concerns adapter training.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss is not tested; only a monotone three-point ablation of frozen encoders inside the authors' method.
No exponents or fitting choices examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 and its V6 supports label are dropped. The encoder-size sweep is an ablation of the authors' method with three uncontrolled points, not a test of downstream scaling predictability. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from smaller-run fits.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests image-text retrieval with encoder-size changes, but not downstream predictability from language-model pretraining loss, a fitted scaling law, or a broad range of downstream tasks.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 & BGE Small
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retrieval performance across paired unimodal encoder sizes
rows.note: The paper groups this point into a sweep labeled S, B, and L and states that scaling the unimodal encoders improves downstream performance.
rows.check: Point in an ablation of the paper's own method (frozen encoder size in FuseMix). It does not measure V6's predictability with scale or loss. Value is figure-only (Fig. 5a, roughly 40–70 R@1 range); baseline not stated.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 & BGE Base
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retrieval performance across paired unimodal encoder sizes
rows.note: The paper groups this point into a sweep labeled S, B, and L and states that scaling the unimodal encoders improves downstream performance.
rows.check: Same as r1: method-ablation point, figure-only value, no fit or predictability measure.

rows.subject: DINOv2 ViT-G/14 & BGE Large
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retrieval performance across paired unimodal encoder sizes
rows.note: The paper groups this point into a sweep labeled S, B, and L and states that scaling the unimodal encoders improves downstream performance.
rows.check: Same as r1. Also, 'L' pairs DINOv2 ViT-G/14 (giant) with BGE Large, so image and text sizes are not scaled in matched steps. This is the largest-config point; Table 1 reports R@1 71.2 for FuseMix(D,B) with the largest encoders.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
